CVE-2026-47430 fleet exposure via Defender TVM (vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) AIReconnaissance High
Direct CVE-keyed asset-discovery hunt against Defender Threat & Vulnerability Management for every device the scanner has tagged as carrying CVE-2026-47430. Drives patch prioritisation for iOS Cordova apps whose host plugin (cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) sits below 6.0.1 and is exploitable via attacker-controlled WebView content. Rationale: The advisory ships CVE-2026-47430 against npm:cordova-plugin-inappbrowser <6.0.1. A direct CveId match against the Defender TVM tables is the cleanest, lowest-FP fleet-exposure inventory — it pivots on the article's primary identifier with no need to model the exploit chain itself. The detection has no FP risk from process-level noise because TVM only flags hosts where the scanner actually identified the affected SoftwareVersion. Cross-checked GHSA URL. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
ATT&CKT1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM scan lag — host already patched but inventory not yet rescanned post-bump
  • Developer workstation with two checkout copies of the same repo (counted twice)
  • Build host with the vulnerable plugin cached under a non-active workspace but no longer used
  • Test fixture intentionally pinned to vulnerable version for the project's own CVE regression suite
  • Defender TVM may not natively map every npm-package CVE — coverage gaps yield false negatives rather than false positives, but means an empty result is not conclusive on its own
Response runbook
1) Triage: per device hit, pull the SoftwareName and SoftwareVersion and verify with a manual `npm ls cordova-plugin-inappbrowser` (or grep the affected workspace's package-lock.json) to rule out stale TVM telemetry. 2) Contain: drive each affected developer / build host to upgrade the plugin to >=6.0.1, rebuild any iOS Cordova app that bundled the old version, and pull / revoke any external TestFlight or App Store builds that shipped a vulnerable bundle. 3) Hunt: cross-reference the affected hostnames against MDM and iOS app-inventory to identify which production user-facing apps actually embedded the vulnerable plugin, then in those apps' identity logs (sign-in, OAuth consent, token refresh) look back 60 days for anomalous behaviour consistent with attacker-driven callback spoofing — unexpected camera/contacts/file plugin invocations from app sessions that opened external URLs in InAppBrowser, or token-refresh storms from a single device.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-47430"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            ObservedVersions = make_set(SoftwareVersion),
            Severity = any(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel),
            RecommendedFix = any(RecommendedSecurityUpdate)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName
| order by LastSeen desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-47430"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            ObservedVersions = make_set(SoftwareVersion),
            Severity = any(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel),
            RecommendedFix = any(RecommendedSecurityUpdate)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName
| order by LastSeen desc
APPLICATION
search index=defender_tvm sourcetype="defender:tvm:vulnerabilities" CveId="CVE-2026-47430"
| stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(SoftwareVersion) as observed_versions values(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel) as severity by DeviceName SoftwareVendor SoftwareName
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - last_seen

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shopper: Authorization bypass and RBAC privilege escalation in team settings

CVEsCVE-2026-47744

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable Shopper admin panel routes — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — including their Livewire AJAX endpoints. Pre-patch (Shopper < 2.8.0) these were reachable by any authenticated panel user and were the only network observable for the authorization-bypass / RBAC privilege-escalation chain disclosed in GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7. Rationale: The article names exactly two Livewire components — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — as the abuse surface. Livewire routes those component names verbatim through /livewire/update (Livewire v3) and /livewire/message/{component} (v2), so the component string and these endpoints are the highest-fidelity strings available pre-exploit. POST/PUT/PATCH on the role-permission route is the specific action that grants/escalates permissions, distinguishing exploitation from normal page loads. No external IOC corroboration was attempted since the advisory exposes no network IOCs — only source-code paths.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Shopper panel administrators (manage_users holders) creating roles or updating role permissions in normal operations
  • Internal QA / penetration-test exercises against the upgraded (>=2.8.0) panel
  • Application monitoring/uptime probes hitting the admin panel index without authentication (will 302 to login but still appear in HTTP logs)
  • Crawlers / bots probing /livewire/update on any Livewire-built site (broad Livewire scanners)
  • Reverse-proxy retries duplicating the same POST to /livewire/update on transient 5xx
Suppression filter
| where not (User in~ ("admin","superadmin") and ClientIP in ("10.0.0.0/8","192.168.0.0/16")) and not (UserAgent has_any ("Pingdom","UptimeRobot","StatusCake"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the Shopper composer.lock from the affected host and confirm shopper/framework < 2.8.0; if patched, downgrade severity. Identify the authenticated session behind the request (panel session cookie or X-Forwarded-User) and map to the panel user — was it a holder of view_users only? 2) Contain: force-logout all panel sessions, rotate panel admin credentials, and either upgrade to shopper/framework 2.8.0 immediately or block /livewire/update and /admin/settings/team* at the WAF until upgrade. 3) Hunt: dump the roles and role_permission tables and diff against a known-good snapshot — look for newly granted manage_users / edit_orders to non-admin accounts; review the panel users table for unexpected deletions of legitimate administrators; pivot on the source IP across the prior 30 days for any other panel reconnaissance.
// Requires IIS / nginx access logs ingested to a custom table; M365 Defender XDR does not natively capture inbound HTTP to a self-hosted PHP app.
// Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for the web server's inbound traffic to the panel's listening port, then triage in the proxy/WAF.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where Connections > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["settings/team","settings.team.index","settings.team.role-permission","settings.team.rolepermission","/livewire/update","/livewire/message/settings.team"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, Method=csMethod, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status=scStatus, ClientIP=cIP, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or CsUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Computer=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Url=strcat(CsUriStem, iff(isnotempty(CsUriQuery), strcat("?", CsUriQuery), "")), Status=ScStatus, ClientIP=CIp, UserAgent=UserAgent, User=CsUsername),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Computer=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), ClientIP=SourceIP, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName)
)
| where Method in~ ("POST","PUT","PATCH") or Url has_any ("role-permission","rolepermission")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Methods = make_set(Method), Statuses = make_set(Status), UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Users = make_set(User, 10) by ClientIP, Computer, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-47731: NASA AMMOS Instrument Toolkit: Path traversal

Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) AIExploitation High
Hunts the actual exploit shape against the AIT-Core BSC HTTP API: POST to /<name>/start carrying attacker-controlled log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, or path form fields with path-traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, absolute paths like /etc, /home, /root). Pre-patch AIT-Core <3.1.1 and <2.6.1 lets an unauthenticated remote caller use these fields to redirect log_file writes anywhere ait-bsc can write — corruption of .py modules then yields RCE on next restart. Rationale: Targets the exact REST shape from the article (the Bottle route `/<name>/start` registered in `StreamCaptureManagerServer._route()`) plus the three attacker-influenced form fields named in the bug write-up (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) combined with traversal markers (../ %2e%2e absolute /etc /root /home). The article confirms there is no auth on the route and these fields go straight into `os.path.join` without realpath canonicalisation. Cross-checked against the GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 advisory and the AIT-Core 3.1.1/2.6.1 patch notes which scope the same parameter list. Falcon FDR doesn't natively ship HTTP request bodies so falcon_logscale_query is empty; the same telemetry is covered by NetworkConnectIP4 in UC2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/releases/tag/3.1.1
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Burp Pro) probing the BSC endpoint as part of a sanctioned scan
  • Mission-ops engineers running `python_poc.py` from the AIT-Core test harness against a lab BSC instance
  • Custom ground-system tooling that legitimately passes log_dir_path to relocate captures between mission phases
  • Health-check probes that POST malformed bodies to /start to verify the route is alive (yields 400 but trips URL pattern)
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIp in ("10.", "172.16.", "192.168.") and UA has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","Burp","Acunetix","Nmap")) and not (Uri endswith "/healthcheck/start")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full POST body from the proxy/WAF capture, decode the form fields, and verify whether log_dir_path / path resolves outside the configured `root_log_directory` from bsc.yaml. Pivot on `source IP` to see whether the same caller hit /stats or other handler names. Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter and stop the ait-bsc systemd unit (`systemctl stop ait-bsc`) — do NOT just kill the process because gevent greenlets can keep writing in an infinite-loop bug mentioned in the advisory. Hunt: review DeviceFileEvents for writes by python/ait-bsc into /etc, /root, /home/*/.ssh, site-packages/ait/, or any *.py outside the project tree in the previous 24h; verify SHA256 of any AIT-Core .py against the package wheel hashes; check for outbound TCP from ait-bsc to non-baseline destinations (see related UC2).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionFound","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), AnyLocalPort=any(LocalPort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TraversalTokens = dynamic(["log_dir_path","file_name_pattern","..%2F","..%2f","..%5C","..%5c","%2e%2e","path=%2F","path=/etc","path=/root","path=/home","path=/var","path=/tmp","log_dir_path=/"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog

ait-bsc outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination (attacker-supplied loc port) AICommand & Control High
Detects ait-bsc / python processes running the ait.core.bsc StreamCaptureManager opening outbound TCP/UDP sessions to non-RFC1918, non-baseline destinations. Per CVE-2026-47731 the unauth /<name>/start endpoint lets a remote caller supply arbitrary `loc` + `port` form values which BSC dutifully `gevent.spawn`s a socket against — making BSC initiate egress to attacker-controlled infrastructure that then streams attacker-chosen bytes back into the file append sink. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-confirmed primitive: the attacker controls `loc` and `port` in the form body and BSC `gevent.spawn`s a SocketStreamCapturer at that endpoint — i.e. BSC initiates the egress under attacker direction. Process-context match uses the exact module path (`ait.core.bsc`), class name (`StreamCaptureManagerServer`), and config file (`bsc.yaml`) shown in the source excerpt. Sentinel query splits process-context resolution onto ImProcessCreate (which carries ActingProcessCommandLine) and joins by DvcHostname into ImNetworkSession (which does not) — the schema-correct way to express the same logic the Defender query expresses inline. Cross-checked against GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 patch diff which restricts socket creation to validated paths only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/blob/main/ait/core/bsc.py
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1659
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ground-station configurations where BSC connects to a public-IP downlink receiver (rare, but check bsc.yaml first)
  • Mission-ops sites running ait-bsc against a cloud-hosted relay (AWS Ground Station, Azure Orbital) which presents as a public IP
  • Engineer testing against a remote development BSC server over a tunnel that egresses to the tunnel endpoint's public IP
  • Updates / pip installs run from the same venv where ait-bsc is installed (mitigated by the process-name filter, but pip can shell into python entrypoints)
Suppression filter
| where not (DstIpAddr in ("<known_ground_station_ip_1>","<known_ground_station_ip_2>")) and not (DstPortNumber in (8080, 8443) and BscCommandLine has "--allow-public-relay")
Response runbook
Triage: pull bsc.yaml from the host and confirm the destination IP+port is NOT in the configured handler list — any unrecognised loc is high-fidelity evil. Capture the BSC handler stats endpoint output (`GET /stats`) to enumerate every currently registered logger and their loc/port/path. Contain: stop the ait-bsc service and revoke any open TCP socket — note the advisory warns of an infinite-loop write bug on close, so plan disk-space monitoring during teardown. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for writes by the same ait-bsc PID within the same window, especially to .py / .sh / authorized_keys / cron paths; verify all AIT-Core site-packages files match the wheel hash; pivot the remote IP across DNS / proxy logs to find other internal hosts that reached out to it.

| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), DistinctRemotes=dcount(RemoteIP) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc

Hunts HTTP POST requests to the DbGate /runners/load-reader endpoint carrying an injection-shaped functionName (newline + import('child_process') + execSync). Article-specific to the unsanitized template interpolation in packages/api/src/controllers/runners.js. and not SourceIP in ("<scanner-cidr>", "<redteam-ip>") and not csUserName in~ ("dbgate-ci", "dast-bot")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body for the matching session, decode any URL-encoded newlines, and confirm functionName contains a newline plus child_process/import/execSync. Identify the authenticated DbGate user from the JWT and the source IP. 2) Contain: revoke the DbGate user's credentials, rotate any DB connection passwords referenced in DbGate config, block the source IP at the proxy, and snapshot the DbGate container for forensics before restart. 3) Hunt: from the same source IP and same authenticated user, pivot to UC2 (node spawning shell), egress connections from the DbGate container, and any FileWritten events under /tmp/_rce_* or other UUID-suffixed paths that match the PoC's jslout pattern.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/runners/load-reader" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/runners/load-reader"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectMarkers = dynamic(["child_process","execSync","await import","%0A","\\nvar ","\\nawait"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem endswith "/runners/load-reader"
  | extend Payload = strcat(csUriQuery, " ", csUserAgent)
  | where Payload has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST" and RequestURL has "/runners/load-reader"
  | where RequestURL has_any (SuspectMarkers) or Message has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "POST" and Url has "/runners/load-reader"
  | where Url has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DbGate node process spawning shell child (post-exploit RCE) AIInstallation High
Hunts for the dbgate / node.js process spawning a shell or command interpreter, which is the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-47670's child_process.execSync call. The legitimate DbGate runtime does not spawn /bin/sh or cmd.exe as children, so any such child is suspicious in container or host context. Rationale: DbGate's normal runtime never spawns a POSIX shell or Windows command interpreter — the article explicitly states the bypass is `(await import('child_process')).execSync(...)`, so child-process creation under a node parent named dbgate is the direct execution-time signal. Pairs with UC1 to give one network-side and one host-side detection of the same chain.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DbGate plugin or admin shell-out feature in a customized fork (verify against vendor binary)
  • DbGate container's entrypoint script invoking sh at startup (filter on container start time)
  • Backup / cron sidecars that exec sh inside the dbgate container's PID namespace
  • Developer attaching to the dbgate pod via kubectl exec (filter by InitiatingProcessCommandLine containing 'docker-exec' or by interactive TTY)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker-entrypoint.sh","yarn start","npm start") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c","node "))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full child cmdline and walk back to the parent node process. If the cmdline matches recon (id, whoami, uname -a) or contains base64/curl/wget, treat as confirmed RCE. Correlate with UC1 within the same 60s window from the same DbGate instance. 2) Contain: kill the dbgate container/pod, isolate the host, rotate the DbGate admin password and any DB credentials in DbGate's connection store (LOGIN_PASSWORD_*, PASSWORD_con*). 3) Hunt: pivot on the dbgate host's outbound network connections in the prior hour, look for /tmp/_rce_*.jsonl style file writes referenced in the PoC, search for newly created users / SSH keys, and check the DB engines DbGate had connections to for follow-on activity from the dbgate host's IP.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","dbgate","dbgate.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/app/packages/api", "/dbgate", "dbgate")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","busybox","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(node|dbgate)(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "dbgate"
  | where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash|busybox|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh(\.exe)?)$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","dbgate.exe") 
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessName in~ ("auditd","audit")
  | where SyslogMessage has "type=EXECVE" and SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/bin/dash")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any ("node","dbgate")
  | project TimeGenerated, HostName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
